analysis: Docs-only PR touching docs/architecture/security/provider-trust.md (date bump at line 3, new paragraph at head lines 128-137) and docs/developer/build.md (new SDK 27.2 Date comparison guidance at head 180-192, shown in the patch). No code, workflow, authorization, key-handling, or deployment changes are present. Security-relevant claims were checked against TB-011, T-057 and TB-002. The new text says a crash loop on pre-release macOS 27.2 builds (26B5091g) leaves App Attest pending and relaxes no authorization. That matches the threat model's fail-closed posture: expiry or unavailable evidence never extends App Attest permission, and the crash adds no trust. A provider crash loop is an availability concern already covered by T-057 (a provider stranded without authorization), and it is described as a limitation rather than a new gap. Nothing in the PR weakens the authorization boundary. Two controls the docs name were not in the supplied evidence: scripts/check-date-comparisons.py (the docs themselves say it has no types and can miss a comparison) and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py (nm/otool checks on built binaries). I could not verify that these scripts exist, that CI wiring is correct, or that they work as described. The docs' claim that the release build refuses affected binaries is therefore unverified. This is an integration question about the build-hardening contract, not a security finding. The wording that App Attest key-generation budget, enrollment resume, stall restart and key history checks are the affected checks was not verified against the Swift source. No threat-model updates are needed: the existing T-057 availability coverage is sufficient.
